title: DeAndre Jordan on CP3's Legacy, Derik Queen's Growth
htmlContent:
DeAndre Jordan has seen just about everything in his 19 NBA seasons. He has been an All-Star, an All-NBA center, an Olympic gold medalist, and an NBA champion. He also spent six seasons catching lobs from one of the greatest point guards the game has ever seen.

Now a veteran leader with the New Orleans Pelicans, Jordan spoke with LandonBuford.com about Chris Paul's career and retirement, his own plans for life after basketball, and the progress of Pelicans big man Derik Queen.

"His Resume Speaks for Itself"

Jordan and Paul were the backbone of the "Lob City" Los Angeles Clippers, teaming up from 2011 to 2017 alongside Blake Griffin. Those Clippers teams turned one of the league's most overlooked franchises into a perennial playoff team and one of the most entertaining shows in basketball.

When asked about Paul, Jordan didn't hesitate.

"Chris is obviously, his game, his resume speaks for itself," Jordan said. "What he's done on and off the basketball floor has been amazing. Nothing short of it."

Jordan credited Paul with playing a major role in his own development.

"Obviously, we had some great years together, and he helped me tremendously throughout my career," he said. "He's had an amazing career. Individually, first-ballot Hall of Famer. I'm extremely proud of the career he's had, and I'm happy for him."

Not the Ending Paul Wanted

Paul's final NBA season did not go according to plan. After returning to the Clippers in the summer of 2025 for what was expected to be a farewell tour, he was sent homefrom a road trip in Atlanta in early December. He was later traded to the Toronto Raptors at the deadline, waived and announced his retirement in February, ending a 21-year career.

Jordan acknowledged that it was not the exit anyone hoped to see.

"Going into retirement, obviously, probably wasn't the way that he wanted to go out of the NBA, and the fans wanted him to go out," Jordan said. "But that's just what it is right now."

Still, Jordan said his former teammate is making the most of his new chapter.

"He's enjoying it," Jordan said. "He gets to play a little bit more golf."

Should the Clippers Retire His Jersey?

The Clippers have yet to retire a jersey in franchise history. Many around the league view Paul as the strongest candidate to be the first, despite the messy ending to his second stint with the team.

Jordan believes the franchise has to be considering it.

"I mean, it's kind of hard not to think that that is something that they're thinking about," Jordan said. "When he came to the Clippers, he helped change the culture and the trajectory of that franchise, and he did so many great things. But I don't know. We'll see what happens."

Before Paul arrived in 2011, the Clippers had rarely been relevant. With Paul running the show, they became a consistent winner and a must-watch team. That history is a big part of the case for his No. 3 one day hanging in the rafters.

Business After Basketball

At 38, Jordan is one of the oldest players in the NBA. The Pelicans brought him back over the summer for his 19th season, and he knows the end of his playing days is coming at some point. But he isn't ready to slow down just yet.

"I'm rounding it all in at some point, but I'm just having so much fun competing, helping the young guys," Jordan said. "I still got that fire in my belly when it comes to competition and getting better and wanting to compete and try to win."

Jordan has been building his portfolio away from the court for years, including his involvement with Players TV. He made it clear that he is staying busy, while keeping his focus on the game for now.

"I got some things going on, but I'm taking it one day at a time," he said. "I definitely got a lot of stuff going on outside of basketball, but I'm focusing on my main job right now, which is basketball. But I'm definitely preparing."

Watching Derik Queen Grow

One of the reasons Jordan is still enjoying the grind is the chance to mentor young players like Derik Queen.

The Pelicans traded up to select Queen out of Maryland with the 13th pick in the 2025 NBA Draft. He went on to earn NBA All-Rookie Second Team honors after a rookie season that included a 30-point triple-double before his 21st birthday.

Queen also had his share of growing pains, including stretches on the bench as the Pelicans struggled through a difficult season. Through it all, Jordan has been right there with him in practice every day.

His assessment was short and to the point.

"Derik is great," Jordan said. "He's improved."

Coming from a veteran who learned the game next to Chris Paul and has battled the league's best bigs for nearly two decades, that is meaningful praise.
excerpt: DeAndre Jordan spoke with LandonBuford.com about Chris Paul's career and retirement, whether the Clippers should retire Paul's jersey, his own plans for life after basketball, and the development of Pelicans rookie Derik Queen.
